# Segment trees

A segment tree stores information about intervals. Each node owns a
segment, and its value is computed by merging its two children.

```text
           [1,8]
      /             \
   [1,4]           [5,8]
  /     \          /     \
[1,2]  [3,4]    [5,6]  [7,8]
```

If the merge is associative, such as `min`, `max`, `sum`, `gcd`, or
a custom dynamic-programming state, a range query can be decomposed
into `O(log n)` tree nodes.

# Point update and range query

For point assignment, update one leaf, then recompute ancestors on
the path to the root. This costs `O(log n)`. Range minimum queries
use `merge = min`.

Example with 1-based array:

```text
a = [7, 2, 6, 3]
```

Leaves store:

```text
[1,1]=7  [2,2]=2  [3,3]=6  [4,4]=3
```

Internal minimum nodes:

```text
[1,2]=min(7,2)=2
[3,4]=min(6,3)=3
[1,4]=min(2,3)=2
```

If `a[2]` becomes `8`, only nodes on the leaf-to-root path change:

```text
[2,2], [1,2], [1,4]
```

This is why updates are logarithmic.

# Rich node states

Segment trees are powerful because a node can store more than one
number. For maximum subarray sum, each node stores:

```text
sum   = total sum of the segment
pref  = best non-empty prefix sum
suff  = best non-empty suffix sum
best  = best non-empty subarray sum
```

To merge left `L` and right `R`:

```text
sum  = L.sum + R.sum
pref = max(L.pref, L.sum + R.pref)
suff = max(R.suff, R.sum + L.suff)
best = max(L.best, R.best, L.suff + R.pref)
```

This is a recurring red-level idea: design exactly the information
that makes two halves composable.

# Lazy propagation

If an update covers a whole node segment, do not immediately walk
into all leaves. Store a pending tag on the node. For range-add and
range-sum:

```text
seg[node] += delta * segment_length
lazy[node] += delta
```

Before visiting children, push the tag to them. Lazy propagation
turns range update plus range query from `O(n)` to `O(log n)`.

# Why the maximum-subarray state works

When two neighboring segments are merged, the best subarray in the union is one
of exactly three types:

```text
entirely in left
entirely in right
crosses the boundary
```

The crossing case must be:

```text
best suffix of left + best prefix of right
```

That is why the node stores `pref` and `suff` in addition to `best`.

# Lazy propagation example

Suppose a node covers `[5,8]` and stores sum `20`. Adding `+3` to the whole
range changes the sum by:

```text
4 positions * 3 = 12
new sum = 32
```

We record `lazy += 3` and stop. If a later query needs `[5,6]`, we push the tag
to children before descending:

```text
left child [5,6]  gets +3 on 2 positions
right child [7,8] gets +3 on 2 positions
```

The parent tag is then cleared.

# Mistakes to avoid

```text
Mixing inclusive and half-open ranges.
Forgetting that maximum subarray is non-empty in this section.
Applying lazy delta to seg[node] without multiplying by segment length.
Not pushing lazy tags before descending into a partially covered node.
```
# Local exercises

- A. Range Minimum Updates: Point-assign values and answer range minimum queries.
- B. Maximum Subarray Updates: After each point assignment, print the maximum non-empty subarray sum of the whole array.
- C. Lazy Range Add Sum: Support range add updates and range sum queries.

# How to use the checker

The local checker compiles/runs both languages and compares output tokens
exactly:

```bash
CP_TARGET=solution python3 sections/37_segment_trees/check.py
```

Replace `CP_TARGET=solution` by your own `solve.cpp` or `solve.py` attempts
when practicing.
